subject: Region presets & delegated erasures — action plan
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@medidatahealth.org>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Region presets & delegated erasures — questions

Hi Soojin,

Quick question as we're finalizing our procurement checklist: does Redwood support per-organization (workspace-level) region presets so that new customer data is pinned to a specific geo by default? Our security team wants to avoid per-request region selection and have an enforcement point at provisioning.

Separately, we have a use case where workspace admins should be able to request account-scoped erasures (e.g., decommissioning entire tenant data after contract termination). Is that something their admin can trigger in-console (self-serve) or would Redwood need to perform the erase on our behalf? We also need clarity on audit logs, proof of deletion, and expected SLA for completing full-data erasure once requested.

Happy to jump on a quick call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Security Operations
Medidata Health

Attachment: medidata-presets-scope.xlsx (spreadsheet: current org defaults + compliance notes)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@medidatahealth.org>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Region presets & delegated erasures — questions

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear breakdown and the attachment (I pulled the sheet). This is exactly the sort of requirement we want to support as a first-class capability. High-level options we can offer: 

- "Organization presets": per-workspace default region binding at provisioning time. This would surface in the admin UI + provisioning API so customers can pin their data path to a region.
- "Admin-initiated erasure": two modes — self-serve (admin triggers erasure via Console/API and receives a signed audit token + deletion manifest) or assisted (customer requests and we execute with audit log).
- Proof of deletion + SLA: we can provide verifiable deletion manifests (hashes + timestamps) and map to an effort-level SLA (MVP: 30 days; expedited: 5 business days with an ops runbook).

Technical asks for product/eng: see inline Qs below — @Karthik can you confirm feasibility and high-level ETA? @Lauren can you advise on priority (SOC2/contract-driven deals vs. self-serve roadmap)?

Action items / clarifying questions: 
1) Should region binding be immutable after creation, or should we allow a migration path that moves data to a new region? (Medidata: preference = immutable)
2) For self-serve erasure, do we need a legal hold snapshot option (retain for X days but mark inaccessible) before final purge? (Medidata: they might request 30-day legal hold)
3) What level of audit detail is required (per-file object hash vs. per-tenant manifest)?

I attached a short proposal PDF to capture the above and suggested flows for Console/API. Happy to set a 30-minute sync this week.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Product Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-region-presets-proposal.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 24 Jun 2028 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Region presets & delegated erasures — feasibility notes

Thanks — dug into implementation tradeoffs and rough schedule. Key points: 

- Region-binding approach: introduce a tenant metadata flag (region_id) at provisioning. This is cheap from a routing perspective but we must ensure the storage tier and KV cache honor the flag. Current cache layer assumes global keyspace; we'll need a cache-partitioning change to avoid cross-zone reads on cold starts.
- Migration path: possible but non-trivial. Full region migration requires cross-region copying + index rebuild + consistent cutover. Recommend "immutable by default" for MVP, with a migration job planned for v2.
- Erasure pipeline: 3-stage delete (mark-for-delete -> background purge -> final manifest) to support legal holds and provide time-bounded rollback for accidental deletes. Final manifest generation (with object hashes + deletion timestamps) is feasible but requires indexing of object hashes during writes (adds ~5-8% overhead).
- SLA estimates: MVP self-serve erase (console trigger + manifest generation) ~ 8 weeks (small team + infra work). Full safe-delete with expedited ops path and multi-region verifiable manifests ~ 14 weeks.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Cache invalidation complexity for in-flight sessions: mitigate with per-tenant eviction hooks and a short rolling invalidation window.
- Cost: storing per-object hashes increases storage/IO; propose an opt-in "forensic mode" for accounts that require forensic manifests.

Next steps: engineering plan doc (I started a draft) and pick two canary customers for an internal pilot. I'll add the draft link to our shared doc collection.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Related link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b-region-presets-plan (engineering draft)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@medidatahealth.org>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Region presets & delegated erasures — action plan

Hi Elena — following up with a proposed plan based on engineering feedback: 

Summary for Medidata: 
- We will ship an "Organization region preset" (immutable at create) in the next roadmap slice — this ensures new workspaces for Medidata will be pinned to your selected US region by default.
- Self-serve admin erasure will be available as an MVP: admin triggers erasure in Console, the system performs a three-stage deletion and produces a signed deletion manifest. Target timeline for Medidata pilot: 8–10 weeks.
- For customers requiring verifiable per-object manifests and expedited SLAs, we'll offer an opt-in forensic mode and an assisted ops pathway (full safe-delete) — delivery in the following release (~14 weeks).

Proposed next steps: 
1) Quick scoping call (30 min) next Tue/Wed to confirm Medidata's legal-hold window and decide whether to enable forensic mode for the pilot.
2) We'll open HS-0004123 in HubSpot and use it for tracking; I'll attach the pilot acceptance criteria and timeline.
3) Karthik will run a short infra readiness spike and share a checklist for canary onboarding.

If that aligns, I'll schedule the call and share the pilot document. Thanks again for surfacing this — this feature will also unblock several regulated prospects.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Product Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
